security.finding: SQL injection via string interpolation in SQL queries ('${teamId}', '${email}'); IDOR vulnerability because any authenticated user can invite anyone to any team without admin/membership authorization.

edge_cases.finding: Missing validation on email format/null/empty; missing check for existing team membership or self-invitation; unvalidated teamId format.

error_handling.finding: Catch block swallows error details with console.log; no transaction rollback if emailService.send fails after database insert, leaving orphaned pending invitations.

naming_and_abstractions.finding: createInvitation violates single responsibility by orchestrating validation, persistence, and external email dispatch; SELECT * query when only name is needed; log line leaks internal topology.

test_coverage.finding: Single happy-path test with tautological mock returning identical payload for both queries; zero assertions on query parameters, payload body, or error paths.

mental_model: Pattern completion in LLMs naturally defaults to high-probability tokens (the happy path). Defensive code (authorization barriers, rollback logic, edge case validation) represents statistically lower probability paths that human senior engineers must systematically inspect and enforce.
